statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00Z on Friday and reopen only at 22:00Z on Sunday, so no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any hour of this 24-hour horizon, which ends about three hours before that reopen. Stress is 40, moderate: a 50% US tariff on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods is in force with talks suspended and a dollar-for-dollar match dated to 8 September, the latest H.15 column stands at 4.19% on the 2-year, 4.69% on the 10-year and 5.23% on the 30-year with the long end at its highest since 2007, and next week carries PCE, the second GDP estimate, Nvidia's results and a first Jackson Hole keynote from the current Fed Chair. Confidence is 86, high, because every index, volatility, yield, energy, venue and calendar input was re-verified against primary sources this hour, with one quote page returning an index level inconsistent with its own ETF and composite prints and resolved against two independent sources.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered the entire decline to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, below its own open and up 0.33% on the day, while QQQ closed 0.35% higher at 713.44 and VIX settled at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Cross-asset tone into the halt was mixed rather than aligned, with software sectors firm, semiconductors 0.31% lower and megacaps split five to three. Because the venue is shut, no hour in this horizon can generate the shallow-pullback or extreme-holding behaviour that would move Tail toward the block threshold, so Tail stays at its closed-venue floor while Stress carries the unpriced policy and rates stack. The danger window is empty by construction: there is no tradable interval inside the published horizon.
headline: Closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across all twenty-four published hours, the 50% US tariff on Canadian goods completes its first full day unpriced against a 30-year yield at its highest since 2007, and Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run from 2026-08-22T19:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T18:00:00Z and end roughly three hours before that reopen. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session and the close finished below the open, which is the shape of a market that still mean-reverts. One widely used quote page returned an inconsistent Nasdaq-100 level this hour, and the 29,308.86 close was confirmed against QQQ at 713.44 up 0.35%, a Nasdaq Composite close of 26,180.45 up 0.43% and independent session reporting. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range rather than at a stressed extreme, and WTI was last quoted near $87.06, up 0.26%. The dominant unpriced item is trade policy: talks between Washington and Ottawa collapsed shortly before the Friday midnight deadline, a 50% US tariff on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods took effect, and Prime Minister Carney suspended negotiations while dating a dollar-for-dollar response to 8 September, outside this horizon. The rates backdrop is the second unpriced item: the latest H.15 column for 20 August shows 4.19% at two years, 4.69% at ten and 5.23% at thirty, with the long end at its highest since 2007 and the Treasury doubling long-bond buybacks to at least $4bn per operation from 9 September, a step that has drawn the Fed-independence debate into the rates discussion. Company-level weekend flow is single-name rather than index-level: Tesla is recalling about 2.98m vehicles in China over door releases, yet the stock closed the Friday session 5.14% higher. The Strait of Hormuz shipping constraint persists without fresh escalation this weekend. Next week carries a dense checkpoint stack outside this horizon: consumer confidence, new home sales and a 2-year auction on 25 August, PCE and the second GDP estimate on 26 August alongside Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 results after the close, jobless claims and a 7-year auction on 27 August, and the first Jackson Hole keynote from the current Fed Chair on 28 August. None of that can be expressed as a Nasdaq-100 price path before this forecast expires, which is why the whole stack sits in Stress and the forward calendar while Tail holds its closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 22 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z and 06:00Z clock-hours on 22 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout, so no hour approached the block threshold. The path tracks the transition from the live Friday session, where Tail ran 10-16 and Stress 48-54 with a mixed dominant mode, into the futures halt at 21:00Z, after which Tail fell to the closed-venue floor of 4 and the dominant mode settled to normal. Stress fell with the halt to 35-38 overnight and then rebuilt to 42 through Saturday as the tariff step took effect, easing to 41 in the four most recent hours once the Canadian response was dated to 8 September. Confidence stayed in an 84-88 band throughout.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T18:00:00Z and ends about three hours before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds 4 in every hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON, with the danger window empty because no tradable interval exists inside the horizon. Stress eases from 40 to a trough of 37 through the quiet Saturday evening and overnight hours, then rebuilds to 44 by the final slot as the reopen approaches with the tariff step, a post-2007 long end, the unresolved Hormuz shipping constraint and next week's PCE, GDP, Nvidia and Jackson Hole checkpoints all still unpriced. Confidence decays from 86 to 80 across the horizon purely because the last live price observation ages, not because any source degraded.
